# Known Issues

What is currently wrong, incomplete, or unproven. Published rather than left for you to
discover — a limitation you hear from us costs you ten minutes; the same limitation found
halfway through a project costs you an afternoon and your trust in everything else here.

Accurate as of version 1.0.1471.

---

## Unstable AI engines

**`agy`, `opencode`, `qwen`** throw provider errors noticeably more often
than the rest. Siklab is driving a tool you installed, so when that tool fails mid-run the
symptom reaching you is a build that appears to stall or stop for no reason.

**This is the single most common cause of "Siklab seems broken", and it usually is not.**

**What to do:** switch that agent to `claude` or `codex` in
**Settings → Engines** and run it again. Work already written to disk is kept.

**Status:** partly ours to fix. Siklab should recover from an engine failure more gracefully
than it currently does, and that work is in progress. The provider errors themselves are not
something we control.

---

## Platform coverage

- **macOS (Intel)** — Ships and works, but is not covered by our per-release testing.
- **Linux (arm64)** — Install, start-up, sign-in and the interface are all proven. A full end-to-end build has not been.
- **Linux (x86-64)** — Installed successfully by a beta tester on real WSL. Needs a CPU with AVX2 — the app refuses to start with a named error if yours lacks it.
- **Windows (via WSL2)** — Runs the same Linux build. Does not restart by itself after a reboot — start it again from your WSL terminal.
- **Windows** — There is no native Windows build. Use WSL2.

Full detail on [Requirements](requirements.md).

---

## Everything else currently on the list

- Linux and WSL are beta: a full end-to-end build has not been verified on either.
- macOS on Intel ships but is not covered by our per-release testing.
- Unstable AI CLIs (notably agy, opencode) can throw provider errors mid-build; use claude or codex if a build keeps stalling.
- There is no uninstaller script yet.
- No native Windows build exists.

---

## What this page is not

It is not a statement that everything else works. It is the list of things we know about.
Generated code can still be wrong, and browser verification covers the flows it was asked to
cover — see [What is not guaranteed](requirements.md#what-is-not-guaranteed).

Hit something not listed here? **support@siklabcore.com**, or **Report a problem** from the top bar
in the app. Both help; the in-app one attaches your version and OS automatically.
